strings.sms.race_commands.d_wins_and_it_still_fe: %d wins and it still feels like you haven't peaked yet. That's the scary part.
strings.sms.race_commands.d_wins_you_know_how_bi: %d wins. You know how bitter that makes the rest of the ladder?
strings.sms.race_commands.d_wins_that_s_the_kind: %d wins. That's the kind of total people build whole reputations around.
strings.sms.race_commands.d_wins_on_record_nobod: %d wins on record. Nobody accidentally gets there.
strings.sms.race_commands.d_wins_at_that_point_e: %d wins. At that point even the haters have to get creative.
strings.sms.race_commands.d_starts_in_and_you_ve: %d starts in and you've already got people paying attention. That's how this starts.
strings.sms.race_commands.d_starts_d_wins_d_podi: %d starts, %d wins, %d podiums. You know how stupid that looks to everyone chasing you?
strings.sms.race_commands.d_starts_in_and_you_re: %d starts in and you're already making this feel bigger than a side lane.
strings.sms.race_commands.d_starts_is_enough_for: %d starts is enough for a pattern. You are definitely a pattern now.
strings.sms.race_commands.d_finishes_in_and_the_: %d finishes in and the city still wants more of you. That's a sign.
strings.sms.race_commands.d_finishes_on_file_and: %d finishes on file and you still don't feel settled. That's dangerous in a good way.
strings.sms.race_commands.d_finishes_you_keep_sh: %d finishes. You keep showing up, and that matters more than people admit.
strings.sms.race_commands.yeah_d_rough_one_s_in_: Yeah, %d rough one%s in a row stings. Doesn't erase what you've already built.
strings.sms.race_commands.d_starts_in_and_no_win: %d starts in and no win yet? Fine. That only makes the first one hit harder.
strings.sms.race_commands.already_has_d_clean_be: already has %d clean beats on you and knows exactly how to turn this into a personal race
strings.sms.race_commands.already_has_d_wins_ban: already has %d wins banked and usually knows how to close once they smell the front
strings.sms.race_commands.s_is_the_one_who_can_t: %s is the one who can turn the first phase ugly. %s.
strings.sms.race_commands.s_is_tied_closest_to_y: %s is tied closest to your lane in this one. %s.
strings.sms.race_commands.s_is_the_other_live_na: %s is the other live name on this board. %s.
strings.sms.race_commands.read_sharp_top_end_if_: Read: sharp top end. If %s gets clean air, you're chasing their pace instead of shaping your own race.
strings.sms.race_commands.read_the_launch_is_whe: Read: the launch is where this can go wrong. Keep %s from turning the first phase into noise, then the race should open up.
strings.sms.race_commands.on_this_s_you_re_lined: On this %s, you're lined up with %s.
strings.sms.race_commands.s_is_the_other_name_yo: %s is the other name you do not get to ignore. %s.
strings.sms.race_commands.s_gives_the_field_its_: %s gives the field its bad habit. Enough aggression there to make the launch messy if nobody keeps shape.
strings.sms.race_commands.read_clear_s_early_or_: Read: clear %s early or you spend the whole run reacting instead of dictating.
strings.sms.race_commands.read_if_s_gets_clean_a: Read: if %s gets clean air, you stop racing the field and start racing their shape.
strings.sms.race_commands.s_is_tied_to_you_wheth: %s is tied to you whether you like it or not. %s.
strings.sms.race_commands.s_is_the_other_name_th: %s is the other name that will show up if you hesitate. %s.
strings.sms.race_commands.read_if_s_gets_clean_o: Read: if %s gets clean off the line, you are immediately on the back foot. And if %s turns the launch messy, you're dealing with damage before the race even settles.
strings.sms.race_commands.read_s_is_shaping_the_: Read: %s is shaping the pace, but %s is the one that can break the order if this run gets impatient.
strings.sms.race_commands.at_s_the_run_died_in_t: At %s, the run died in the noise before the flag. That was chaos, not a pace problem.
strings.sms.race_commands.at_s_it_ended_in_a_dnf: At %s, it ended in a DNF. The race never settled long enough to pay back what pace you had.
strings.sms.race_commands.at_s_you_came_from_p_d: At %s, you came from P%d to P%d and took back %d spot%s on clean race pace.
strings.sms.race_commands.at_s_you_still_dragged: At %s, you still dragged it from P%d to P%d through a messy run. Recovery pace held up.
strings.sms.race_commands.at_s_you_slipped_from_: At %s, you slipped from P%d to P%d once the race got dirty. That cost you %d place%s.
strings.sms.race_commands.at_s_you_faded_from_p_: At %s, you faded from P%d to P%d. Read: the pace bled off deeper into the run.
strings.sms.race_commands.at_s_you_held_p_d_beca: At %s, you held P%d because the run stayed clean enough not to leak anything for free.
strings.sms.race_commands.at_s_you_came_home_p_d: At %s, you came home P%d, but the race got loose enough to cap what was really available.
strings.sms.race_commands.s_is_the_mover_in_the_: %s is the mover in the file right now. %s.
strings.sms.race_commands.s_is_the_name_that_kee: %s is the name that keeps leaning into your lane. %s.
strings.sms.race_commands.read_s_has_the_cleanes: Read: %s has the cleanest hold on the tier right now, but the order behind them is still soft enough to move if you hit it clean.
strings.sms.race_commands.s_is_right_there_too_t: %s is right there too. This tier is not a one-name problem.
strings.sms.race_commands.s_took_it_because_s_yo: %s took it because %s. Your run died in the noise before the flag.
strings.sms.race_commands.you_took_this_one_beca: You took this one because the race stayed clean enough to let your pace decide it. %s never got the mess they needed.
strings.sms.race_commands.you_still_took_it_thro: You still took it through the noise. That is control over %s and the rest of the field.
strings.sms.race_commands.s_got_you_here_because: %s got you here because %s. That was race shape, not randomness.
strings.sms.race_commands.s_got_the_better_of_th: %s got the better of this one because %s, then the race broke up and locked the order in.
strings.sms.race_commands.once_that_race_goes_li: Once that race goes live, the long book is mine. You're too late.
